source.title: Training and Scaling Compute-Optimal Physiological Waveform Foundation Models
source.authors: Ping-Zhi Li; Jie Peng; Shu-Qing Luo; Z. Plotkin; Tian-Long Chen

page_placements.theme: Resource-optimal allocation depends on objective, constraints and training stage

record.tranche_reason: It fits and evaluates a scaling law, but on physiological waveform models and downstream clinical ranking error rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study's own results concern scaling and prediction of downstream clinical ranking error. It does not report language-model held-out cross-entropy. Rows summarize results reported for resource configurations or aggregates; cited scaling results from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains over 100 physiological waveform models (20M–2.1B) and fits a scaling law to their downstream clinical ranking error (1 − AUROC). It checks the law at held-out resource levels, at 2.1B and on longer runs. This is the 'other modality / transfer regime' setting of V5. It is a new setting with its own result rather than a different method on LM loss, so T3 fits better than the reader's T2. The study reports no language-model results and no scaling of pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that a law in model size, waveform hours and labeled patients predicts eight-task ranking error: 0.5% MAE held out, 0.9% at 2.1B, 1.0% on longer runs. They say compute-optimal training scales hours much faster than size (10× compute → 1.2× N, 8.2× D). They also say larger models and longer pretraining reduce data and label needs, and that labeled patients are the strongest downstream factor.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses physiological waveform masked reconstruction and frozen linear probes for clinical prediction; it fits a law for ranking error over model size, waveform hours, and labeled patients, rather than language-model next-token cross-entropy over parameters, tokens, and compute.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted downstream-error law implies a compute-optimal allocation of N* ∝ C^0.088 and D* ∝ C^0.912. Data grows far faster than model size, unlike both Kaplan and Hoffmann. The allocation is derived, not trained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal model/data allocation for downstream error in non-text foundation models differs strongly from LM pretraining-loss allocations.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted law implies that doubling N from 25M cuts the waveform hours needed for the same error by 51.8%. Section 5 also derives labeled-patient savings (27.2%, 61%). These are model-derived predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger pretrained models trade off against pretraining data and downstream label requirements at fixed downstream error.

record.problems: The evidence is specific to Aether and eight MIMIC-III clinical tasks. The outcome is downstream ranking error rather than pretraining loss. The reported scaling law is fitted to the study's resource grid; the longer-run and 2.1B evaluations are extrapolations within this setting.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 compare Aether with random initialization and existing baseline FMs; these comparisons do not report the scaling-law prediction outcomes cataloged here. Individual plotted resource configurations in Figures 4–8 are not separately transcribed where the text reports only aggregate prediction errors or ranges.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss. The study's own masked-reconstruction pretraining loss is not reported against N or D.
No extrapolation of LM pretraining loss. Even in the waveform setting, extrapolation in model size is only about 3×.
No LM compute-optimal allocation. The waveform allocation is derived from the fit and not validated with iso-FLOP runs.
Depth and width are tied along a single ladder (Table 1). There is no comparison of shapes at a fixed parameter count.
Pretraining-loss scaling in this modality; image, video and repeated-data regimes; extrapolation over orders of magnitude.
Language-model downstream tasks. The downstream predictability shown here applies to waveform models and is recorded under V5.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting, or schedules.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its outcome is downstream 1 − AUROC with frozen linear probes, not pretraining loss, and the power-law terms act on R/(1−2R) with a multiplicative P^-g factor. The pretraining-data exponent is very small (b = 0.05). Extrapolation in model size is about 2.9×. The compute-optimal allocation comes only from the fitted law, with no iso-FLOP validation, so it should not be read as a test of V3. The record's limits_scope label on V5 described untested parts, not a qualifying result, so it is dropped. The V6 links are dropped because the system is a waveform model, not a language model. All result rows rest on the eight-task mean, with no per-task breakdown of scaling.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss is measured.
No small-run predictions of language-model pretraining loss are evaluated.
The compute-optimal allocation is derived for downstream ranking error in waveform models, not language-model pretraining loss.
The study does not compare depth, width, or architecture details at a fixed parameter count.

It tests a scaling law for downstream clinical ranking error in physiological waveforms, not whether the same law holds for held-out pretraining loss or the other listed modalities and training regimes.
Downstream performance is evaluated on eight clinical tasks using ranking error; other downstream task families and metrics are not tested.
The study does not compare fitting choices or setups to test whether exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on them.

rows.subject: Aether
rows.size_stated: 20M–720M; the fit uses four smaller FMs
rows.stage_stated: pretrained; frozen representations evaluated with linear probes
rows.operation_detail: Fit a scaling law for eight-task mean ranking error using model parameters, pretraining waveform hours, and labeled patients.
rows.measure: Fitted eight-task mean ranking error: R̂ = [2 + P^g/(A N^−a + B D^−b)]^−1; coefficients A = 6931.568, B = 19.421, a = 0.513, b = 0.050, g = 0.296.
rows.note: The fitted outcome is downstream ranking error, not pretraining cross-entropy.
rows.check: This row is fitted coefficients, not an outcome. Its support for V5 rests on Fig. 4a: configurations collapse onto one response curve in S = P^g/(AN^-a+BD^-b). The law is a power-law sum applied to R/(1−2R), not a plain power law in loss. The data exponent is small (b = 0.050). V6 is removed: V6 concerns language-model downstream tasks, and this system is a waveform model, so the evidence enters only through V5.

relationships.condition: Aether physiological waveform models (20M–2.1B), masked-reconstruction pretraining, linear probes, eight-task mean ranking error on MIMIC-III
relationships.reason: One law in N, D and P fits the 140 configurations (r1). It predicts held-out levels with 0.5% MAE (r2), 2.1B with 0.9% MAE (r3) and longer runs with 1.0% MAE (r4). Measured error falls with D and P at 2.1B (r6, r7).
relationships.display_finding: A joint law in N, D and P fit 140 configurations, predicting held-out levels with 0.5% MAE, the 2.1B model with 0.9% MAE and longer runs with 1.0% MAE, while measured error also decreased with D and P at 2.1B.
